batch_contract.timeout_scope: one shared Z3 check-time budget for the whole batch
batch_contract.separation: each returned outer model is separated by an exact full Boolean-assignment blocker
batch_contract.audit: every returned corona is independently verified and then subjected to the accumulated pair, triple, and quadruple audits in sequence
batch_contract.continuation_gate: radius-five GCTS starts only for a model that clears every exact tuple audit
batch_contract.soundness: batch blockers affect only within-call enumeration and are never learned as non-tiling constraints

positive_control.result: The retained-state path processes distinct models in order, learns from one, and can verify a later model through GCTS.

production_probe.result: Blind retained-state enumeration finds one exact proposal but spends the remaining budget without a second. The first model's newly audited pair constraint cannot steer the still-running Python solver, so interactive audit feedback is the next target.

interpretation: Batched enumeration is correct and useful on the positive control, but blind within-formula model blocking does not improve this production seed. It raises the exact pair portfolio to 777 constraints without reaching the full triple audit. The negative throughput result motivates a bidirectional solver session that accepts each exact audit obstruction before requesting the next model; it is not evidence of non-tiling or aperiodicity.
